name: Permanent Neonatal Diabetes Mellitus-Pancreatic and Cerebellar Agenesis Syndrome
aliases: PNDM with Pancreatic and Cerebellar Agenesis
Permanent Neonatal Diabetes with Pancreatic and Cerebellar Hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Permanent Neonatal Diabetes Mellitus Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Onset of diabetes mellitus within the first 6 months of life
Radiological or pathological evidence of pancreatic agenesis or hypoplasia
Neuroimaging confirmation of cerebellar agenesis or severe hypoplasia
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes associated with pancreatic and cerebellar development (e.g., PTF1A)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early-onset diabetes mellitus plus radiological evidence of pancreatic and cerebellar agenesis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and imaging criteria are met.

laboratory: Persistent hyperglycemia with low or absent insulin levels
Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency markers (e.g., low fecal elastase)
imaging: MRI showing absence or severe hypoplasia of the pancreas
Brain MRI demonstrating cerebellar agenesis or hypoplasia
other: Histopathological confirmation of pancreatic agenesis in rare biopsy/autopsy cases

redFlags: Onset of insulin-dependent diabetes within first 6 months of life
Severe intrauterine growth retardation with neurological abnormalities
Imaging evidence of absent pancreas and cerebellum
references: Pinney SE, et al. Permanent neonatal diabetes mellitus due to pancreatic agenesis and cerebellar agenesis. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2011.
Orphanet: Permanent neonatal diabetes mellitus-pancreatic and cerebellar agenesis syndrome. ORPHA:65288.
Stoffers DA. Genetic causes of neonatal diabetes mellitus. Rev Endocr Metab Disord. 2004.
